# 5. Interaction Flow ## 5.1. AN L4 Computing Network Fault Management Workflow The AN L4 fault management framework for computing networks adheres to the I-AADE (Intent-Awareness-Analysis-Decision-Execution) autonomous closed-loop model and aligns with Intent-Based Networking (IBN) principles. Under the constraints of computing and network convergence and end-to-end SLAs, this framework establishes an autonomous fault management closed-loop process across cloud, network, edge, and terminal domains within heterogeneous and dynamic environments. ### Steps 1-2: Fault Occurrence Phase A computing node fault (1) occurs within the computing domain, or a large-scale network fault (2) occurs within the network domain. ### Step 3: Fault Perception Phase The Cross-domain Fault Agent receives proactive data and fault events from the Computing Domain Fault Management Agent (3a) and the Network Domain Fault Management Agent (3b). It also ingests service-layer data/events (3c) and requirements for proactive O&M (3d). ### Steps 4-5: Analysis and Decision Phase The service-layer Cross-domain Fault Agent performs cross-domain correlation analysis (4) to identify fault locations and return links. It then dispatches diagnosis requests and remediation suggestions to the corresponding single-domain Fault Management Agent (5). The resource-layer agents execute self-diagnosis and return results and handling suggestions to the cross-domain agent. ### Steps 6-7: Execution and Remediation Phase If automated remediation is feasible, the resource-layer agent completes the repair and returns the result. If unfeasible, the Cross-domain Fault Agent evaluates the diagnosis and remediation plan; upon confirming automation is impossible, it dispatches the task to the FME via the Work Order System (6). The FME interacts with the service-layer FME Copilot to query equipment info. The service-layer FME Copilot coordinates with the resource-layer FME Copilot, which provides natural language-based operational guidance to assist the FME in completing the fault repair (7). ### Classified Fault Handling Workflows 1. Single-Domain Fault [1/2→3] (Single-Domain Autonomous Loop) The Single-Domain Fault Management Agent automatically identifies, diagnoses, and remediates faults within its own domain. It then reports the execution results, achieving a domain-level autonomous closed-loop. 2. Cross-Domain Fault [1/2→3→4→5] (Cross-Domain Collaborative Loop) Based on the event data reported by single-domain agents, the Cross-domain Fault Agent proactively performs identification and analysis. It automatically extracts fault characteristics, performs fault demarcation, and drives the single-domain agents to execute precise fault localization and remediation. 3. Manual Intervention Required [1/2→3→4→6→7] (Human-in-the-Loop) When the Cross-domain Fault Agent determines that automated remediation is unfeasible based on the reported event data, it escalates the issue by submitting it to the Work Order System. The Copilots provide intelligent assistances for manual troubleshooting, achieving a human-centric closed-loop. ## 5.2.
